metadata.name: Home Network Target Architecture v0.4-simple
metadata.description: v0.4-simple target network architecture. Existing = live; to-buy, planned and future = planned. VLAN 40 is reserved and inactive. Source of truth: homelab-docs/docs/architecture/network-v0.4-simple.md

tiles.title: Internet
tiles.notes: Reached only through the ISP modem/ONT and the ISP WAN. Mullvad and Proton are logical tunnels over that WAN, not separate WANs.

tiles.title: ISP modem / ONT [EXISTING]
tiles.notes: First hop of the only physical Internet path.

tiles.title: Mullvad WireGuard egress tunnel (LOGICAL)
tiles.notes: Logical egress tunnel originating from OPNsense and traversing the ISP WAN. Not a separate physical WAN. Fail closed, no ISP fallback.

tiles.title: OPNsense appliance [TO BUY - model TBD]

fields.role: Only router, firewall, DHCP server, local DNS server, VLAN gateway and commercial VPN gateway

tiles.notes:
WHY: one authority for routing, inter-VLAN policy, DHCP, DNS and VPN egress selection.
Egress: VLAN 10 -> Mullvad; Ugoos AM9 Pro (on VLAN 10, DHCP reservation, policy route) -> Proton; VLAN 30 -> ISP WAN directly; VLAN 60 -> Mullvad; VLAN 50 -> POLICY TBD / per service.
DHCP served for VLAN 10, 30, 50 and 60. Gateway addresses are not assigned yet.

tiles.title: Proton VPN WireGuard egress tunnel (LOGICAL)
tiles.notes: Logical egress tunnel originating from OPNsense and traversing the ISP WAN. Not a separate physical WAN. Fail closed for the Ugoos, no ISP fallback. Local services stay reachable.

tiles.title: VPN fail-closed behaviour

fields.text: Home/Guest: Mullvad down = BLOCKED. Ugoos: Proton down = BLOCKED, local services OK. Direct: always ISP.

tiles.notes:
VLAN 10 Home: Mullvad UP -> via Mullvad. Mullvad DOWN -> Internet BLOCKED. No fallback to ISP.
Ugoos AM9 Pro on VLAN 10: Proton UP -> via Proton. Proton DOWN -> Internet BLOCKED. No fallback to ISP. Local services remain reachable.
VLAN 60 Guest: Mullvad UP -> via Mullvad. Mullvad DOWN -> Internet BLOCKED. No fallback to ISP.
VLAN 30 Direct: always the ISP WAN directly, independent of Mullvad/Proton health.
VLAN 50 Infrastructure: POLICY TBD / per service.

tiles.title: Managed 2.5GbE core switch [TO BUY - model TBD]

fields.uplink: 802.1Q trunk from OPNsense: tagged VLAN 10,30,50,60, no native/untagged VLAN

tiles.notes: WHY: carries the four active VLANs between OPNsense, both APs, the servers, the Ugoos and the desk. Trunks are tagged-only; access ports are untagged.

tiles.title: GL.iNet Flint 2 (GL-MT6000) [EXISTING]

fields.uplink: 802.1Q trunk: tagged VLAN 10,30,50,60, no native/untagged VLAN

tiles.notes: Existing hardware used as an AP/bridge after OPNsense is deployed. Broadcasts Home, Direct and Guest with the same names, security settings and passwords as the Slate Plus.

tiles.title: GL.iNet Slate Plus (GL-A1300) [PLANNED]

fields.uplink: 802.1Q trunk: tagged VLAN 10,30,50,60, no native/untagged VLAN

tiles.notes: Planned specifically as an AP/bridge. Broadcasts Home, Direct and Guest with the same names, security settings and passwords as the Flint 2.

tiles.title: VLAN 10 - Home

fields.egress: Mullvad (fail closed); Ugoos AM9 Pro: Proton

tiles.notes: WHY: trusted household devices. Default Internet egress is Mullvad via OPNsense. VLAN 10 clients may reach selected user-facing services on VLAN 50 such as Jellyfin and Linkwarden. Infrastructure administration interfaces are not generally exposed to all VLAN 10 clients.

tiles.title: SSID Home -> VLAN 10
tiles.notes: Active Wi-Fi SSID.

tiles.title: Ugoos AM9 Pro [EXISTING]

fields.egress: Proton via OPNsense policy route (fail closed)

tiles.notes: Exception to the VLAN 10 default: receives a DHCP reservation and OPNsense policy-routes it through Proton instead of Mullvad. Local services remain reachable. Wired.

tiles.title: MacBook / laptops [EXISTING]
tiles.notes: Existing. Intended ADMIN_DEVICES member later. Linkwarden currently runs here.

tiles.title: GrapheneOS personal phone [EXISTING]
tiles.notes: Existing. Remote private-home access is still under test.

tiles.title: TV [EXISTING] - NO NETWORK
tiles.notes: The TV connects only to the Ugoos via HDMI and stays offline.

tiles.title: Residents' trusted devices
tiles.notes: Residents' trusted phones, tablets and laptops, plus the dual-use work laptop in personal mode.

tiles.title: Remote GrapheneOS / private-home access: UNDER TEST

fields.text: Not finalized. Not part of the target topology.

tiles.notes: Current experiment: WG Tunnel with Mullvad WireGuard. Home Wi-Fi -> device VPN off. Outside home -> Mullvad enabled automatically. Combined private-home WireGuard routing is not finalized and no solution (NetBird or otherwise) is selected.

tiles.title: ADMIN_DEVICES: later / TBD

fields.text: Intended members: Desktop PC and MacBook/admin laptop. Not defined yet.

tiles.notes: ADMIN_DEVICES should later identify the Desktop PC and the MacBook/admin laptop and allow them to reach VLAN 50 administrative interfaces and Synology DSM. Not drawn as firewall links yet.

tiles.title: VLAN 30 - Direct
tiles.notes: WHY: work/corporate VPN, websites that block Mullvad, VPN troubleshooting and temporary direct Internet access. Independent of Mullvad/Proton health.

tiles.title: SSID Direct -> VLAN 30
tiles.notes: Active Wi-Fi SSID. Also wired at the desk.

tiles.title: VLAN 40 - IoT [RESERVED / INACTIVE]
tiles.notes: Do not deploy DHCP, an SSID or firewall configuration yet. Activate only when actual IoT/smart-home devices justify it.

tiles.title: VLAN 60 - Guest
tiles.notes: WHY: Internet-only access for guests. Home, Direct, Infrastructure and future IoT are denied. Wireless client isolation enabled. VPN fails closed with no ISP fallback.

tiles.notes: Active Wi-Fi SSID.

tiles.title: Policy: VLAN 10 Home

fields.text: -> Internet via Mullvad; -> selected VLAN 50 services (Jellyfin, Linkwarden)

tiles.notes:
-> Internet through Mullvad (fail closed)
-> selected user-facing VLAN 50 services such as Jellyfin and Linkwarden: ALLOW
-> infrastructure administration interfaces: not generally exposed
Ugoos AM9 Pro: Internet via Proton instead.

tiles.title: Policy: VLAN 30 Direct

fields.text: -> Internet via ISP, no commercial VPN

tiles.notes: Internet egress is the ISP WAN directly, independent of Mullvad/Proton health. Access to internal networks is not defined in v0.4-simple.

tiles.title: Policy: VLAN 50 Infrastructure

fields.text: VLAN 10 -> selected user services; admin interfaces restricted; egress TBD

tiles.notes: VLAN 10 clients may reach selected user-facing services. Administration interfaces are not generally exposed. ADMIN_DEVICES later. Synology DSM admin restricted. Internet egress: POLICY TBD / per service.

tiles.title: Policy: VLAN 60 Guest

fields.text: Internet via Mullvad only; all internal VLANs denied; client isolation

tiles.notes: Internet allowed. Home denied. Direct denied. Infrastructure denied. Future IoT denied. Wireless client isolation enabled. VPN fails closed with no ISP fallback.

tiles.title: Deferred from v0.3 (not active)

fields.text: VLAN 20 Media and VLAN 99 Management are not active in v0.4-simple

tiles.notes: VLAN 20 Media: the Ugoos moved into VLAN 10 with device-specific Proton routing. VLAN 99 Management: combined into VLAN 50 Infrastructure. Both can be reintroduced later. v0.3 is preserved in homelab-docs (network-v0.3.md and atlas-v0.3.json).

tiles.title: LEGEND
tiles.notes:
Existing hardware uses the live lifecycle; to-buy, planned and future items use planned (with a 'planned' badge). Zones: VLAN 10 blue, 30 orange, 40 grey (reserved), 50 green, 60 yellow.
Lines (cyber theme): white = PHYSICAL ISP WAN path; green = LOGICAL Mullvad tunnel / Mullvad egress; purple = LOGICAL Proton tunnel / Ugoos policy route; blue = 802.1Q trunk; periwinkle = access/wired link; yellow = management; grey = logical relationship; cyan = hosts/runs/SSID. CTRoadmap cannot draw dashed or dotted lines, so logical links are labelled.

tiles.title: Management/recovery access design: TBD before deployment

fields.text: No dedicated recovery path is defined in v0.4-simple

tiles.notes: v0.3 had a dedicated VLAN 99 MGMT / RECOVERY port. VLAN 99 is deferred in v0.4-simple, so the dedicated recovery-management path is unresolved.
